items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: He said "The following agreed to join: Joe Sullivan, Bud Freeman, Floyd O'Brien, Max Kaminsky, Gene Krupa, Eddie Condon and Pee Wee Russell.

ctx.x: He says in August of 1933 he signed a contract with a financial backer to support a mixed Big Band, which had Alex Hill, as the arranger, to front it. This is in Mezzrow's Mezra's book.

He said "The following agreed to join: Joe Sullivan, Bud Freeman, Floyd O'Brien, Max Kaminsky, Gene Krupa, Eddie Condon and Pee Wee Russell. We rehearsed and the future looked good and we were okay for a sustaining program on a network, but soon after, the men in the band left him to go to a rehearsal arranged by Red McKenzie for some other guy who claimed he was a politician's son ..."
Do you remember any of these details? I mean you may not have been around ...

items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: that was a smaller group of some members of your band and some white musicians, namely, Max Kominski [phonetic] and Floyd O’Brien [phonetic]

ctx.x: Well, whatever he thought, I think he had much more to say, and he should have continued.

Then, now we return to that Chocolate Dandies date we mentioned in October of 1933, which was the first recordings with Teddy Wilson, and then a few days later . . . that was a smaller group of some members of your band and some white musicians, namely, Max Kominski [phonetic] and Floyd O’Brien [phonetic] and, reputedly, Mez Mezro [phonetic] banging on the drums somewhere, but that’s not confirmed. But, do you remember, was this another idea of John Hammond, to sort of have an integrated recording unit?
